A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPGT research and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. Added material and reordered appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original PPGT benchmark results in Tables 1–5, component ablations, and appendix experiments on normalization, sensitivity, and runtime.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds a larger-model evaluation and further sensitivity and initialization experiments in Tables 4 and 12–14.

M1.justification: The proposed AdaRMSN, simplified L2 attention, positional-encoding stem, and SPE procedures remain unchanged. Expanded RRWP and Node2Subgraph descriptions document existing components; PPGT-base is another configuration of the retained architecture.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained, including BREC, the graph benchmarks, PCQM4Mv2, OGBN-ArXiv, and the synthetic normalization example. New experiments vary configurations and hyperparameters within existing tasks.

E2.justification: Benchmark comparator membership remains unchanged. However, the new initialization experiment in Table 13 introduces Bad-AdaRMSN, an identity-initialized control, alongside RMSN and normally initialized AdaRMSN.

E3.justification: v4 adds the 86.8M-parameter PPGT-base configuration, with different depth, width, pooling, batch size, and training settings documented in Table 9. New experiments sweep SPE bases, initialization and learning rates over 50 epochs, and sampling depth. These extend evaluation settings without replacing the original benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: The supplementary investigation expands substantially: Table 12 tests SPE sensitivity on ZINC beyond the retained CFI analysis; Table 13 tests initialization-dependent training stability; and Table 14 examines Node2Subgraph depth. These address previously untested practical questions while retaining the original ablations, normalization case study, batch-size analysis, and runtime measurements.

E5.justification: The existing four-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, single-seed PCQM4Mv2 evaluation, and one-tailed significance test remain. The additions introduce no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or explicit increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Table 4 retains the 17.6M-parameter result of 0.0856 MAE as PPGT-small and adds PPGT-base at 0.08396 under different configuration and training settings. Tables 12–14 add SPE sensitivity scores, initialization pass/fail outcomes, and OGBN-ArXiv accuracies from 54.46 to 72.46 across sampling depths. Existing benchmark and figure results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E's propositions and proofs are unchanged. Appendix C.7/Table 16 and D.6 add comparative complexity reasoning, including TokenGT's O((N+ND)^2) = O(N^2D^2) attention cost versus PPGT's O(N^2), plus a formal expressivity comparison.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: minimal Transformer modifications enabling strong graph expressivity and performance, with potential relevance to multimodal models. No central contribution is added or withdrawn.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning model scaling, initialization-dependent stability, regularization for larger SPE basis counts, and dataset-dependent sampling depth. It also qualifies Node2Subgraph as rudimentary. The existing quadratic-complexity limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies a code-access link, documents Node2Subgraph's rollback and frontier-sampling rules, discloses K=15 for the original experiment, and adds PPGT-base hyperparameters. Conversely, Table 9 leaves the OGBN-ArXiv learning-rate and epoch cells blank, whereas v3 supplied them. Other implementation and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix D.6 expands positioning against the already cited TokenGT, discussing tokenization, positional-encoding compatibility, expressivity, computational cost, and the meaning of a plain Transformer. Maron et al. (2018) is newly cited; the broader related-work discussion remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording corrections and explanatory additions, updates publication and author information, and swaps the implementation-details and additional-study appendices from C/B to B/C. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains a model row, Table 9 gains a configuration column, and Tables 12–14 and 16 are added. The original runtime table becomes Table 15. All six original figures retain their graphics, while publication headers, float placement, and pagination change.

improvement.justification: The code pointer, clearer Node2Subgraph procedure, and targeted tests in Tables 12–14 improve reproducibility information and practical validation. These gains are tempered by missing OGBN-ArXiv training cells in Table 9 and a scaling interpretation based on single-seed configurations that differ in several settings. The improvements are useful but limited; the central results and proofs were already present in v3.
